chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali (al-Khazzaj) (al-Washsha') narrated from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him saying: 'Verily, the Prophet Ayyub (peace be upon him) said: O Lord, I have never asked You for anything of this world, ever.' And an inkling of self-admiration entered his heart. Then a cloud approached him and called out to him: 'O Ayyub, who enabled you to do this?' He said: 'You, O Lord.'

key_terms.رِيَاءٌ: Showing off / Self-admiration (implied by context of ودخله شيء)

ai.seo_question: What was the subtle flaw in Prophet Ayyub's supplication that was pointed out by the cloud?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, the Prophet Ayyub (Job) reflects on his supplications, identifying a subtle undercurrent of self-admiration (*riya'*) that accompanied his requests for worldly matters. The divine cloud’s question, 'Who empowered you for this?', serves as a profound reminder that even the capacity to ask is a gift from God, thereby purifying the intention from hidden pride. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on scrutinizing the inner state of the heart during worship to ensure pure monotheistic devotion.
